answer: A verifiable delay protocol mitigates Sybil attacks across agent networks, such as robotic swarms monitoring an alpine meadow or river basin. Agents must compute sequential cryptographic proofs to maintain active identities, rendering zero-cost persona creation a technical fable. An attacker must dedicate scarce, non-parallelizable CPU core-time and electricity per identity. However, this imposes activation latency on honest agents and fails against adversaries with custom ASIC hardware.
